statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = -\left(3s+2t+2u\right), y = 5s-3t+2u, z = 3s+2t-5u.

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} -3 \amp -2 \amp -2\\ 5 \amp -3 \amp 2\\ 3 \amp 2 \amp -5 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries -3,-2,-2 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((-3)(-5)-(2)(2))-3 + ((2)(3)-(5)(-5))-2 + ((5)(2)-(-3)(3))-2 = -133.
